subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native generic provider key/profile quota-bucket routing contract for Gemini-style project quotas, and should it live in core provider/auth fallback or in an external sidecar/plugin seam?
rationale: The remaining work changes public config, auth-profile state, provider selection, cooldown scope, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not invent the product boundary.

options.title: Design generic bucket routing
options.body: Define an additive core/provider contract for quota-bucket metadata and cooldown state, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

options.title: Fold into provider-pool tracker
options.body: Treat this as a narrower acceptance criterion under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 while preserving this issue's Gemini project-bucket evidence.

options.title: Keep external for now
options.body: Recommend the sidecar/plugin approach until maintainers decide native bucket routing is worth the new config and state surface.

recommendation.title: Design generic bucket routing
recommendation.body: Define an additive core/provider contract for quota-bucket metadata and cooldown state, then implement Gemini as one consumer while keeping current flat rotation as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is product/config direction across provider routing and auth state, where steipete has the strongest routing signal among the identified owners.
